subject: Re: Synthetix Labs throughput commit validation & safety headroom
messages:
From: Ethan Locke <ethan.locke@synthetixlabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gutierrez <maria.gutierrez@synthetixlabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput commit validation & token SLOs

Hi Lauren,

Great demo earlier — thanks. Finance and infra are aligned to move toward a Dedicated commitment but we need a short, concrete mapping from our projected traffic to the Dedicated slabs you'd provision so procurement can approve the spend. High-level context: our UAT traffic looks like ~45K tokens/sec sustained during a 20-minute daily job, and peak spikes to ~120K tokens/sec for short bursts (1–3 minutes) around heavy user events. Generation is the heavy part (approx 70% generation / 30% NLU).

Key asks:
- Can Redwood map these numbers to an estimated Dedicated GPU count (preferred H100/Hopper) with a p95 latency SLO target of <= 300ms for generation calls?
- What's recommended headroom (safety factor) for steady-state vs burst?
- Any fallbacks you recommend if Dedicated is saturated (model variant, routing to hosted pool)?

I've attached the peak profile export and a small summary from our analytics. We need a one-page capacity recommendation and an ops-friendly SOW line item that procurement can approve this week.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Locke
Head of Platform
Synthetix Labs
[Attachment: synthetix_peak_profile.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Locke <ethan.locke@synthetixlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput commit validation & token SLOs

Hi Ethan — thanks for the data and the clear asks. We reviewed the export and sketched a preliminary plan. Summary up front: for the observed steady-state (~45K tps) plus 1.5x steady headroom and the short bursts to 120K tps, our recommended starting Dedicated commitment is 6 H100 nodes with burst capacity policy to autoscale an additional 2 H100-equivalent slots from a shared burst pool. That maps to estimated p95 generation latency of ~220–280ms under your traffic mix (70/30), assuming model compiles with 8-bit quantization and standard KV cache behavior.

Open clarifying items that change the mapping:
- Exact model family & context window (we assumed a 8k context generation model similar to MPTX-8k).
- Distribution of request sizes — peak estimate assumes 75% short responses (<512 tokens) and 25% long completion flows.

I've attached a brief prelim estimate (PDF) and included internal notes below for provisioning/ops simulation. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow so we can finalize the SOW verbiage for procurement?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_prelim_gpus_estimate.pdf (pdf)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Throughput commit validation & token SLOs — modeling notes (internal)

Ben/Irene — forwarding Ethan's profile and our prelim. Quick modeling assumptions and asks for Ops/Runtime bench: please validate the following and push back if any number seems optimistic.

Assumptions used for the 6 H100 recommendation:
- Model: gen-heavy, 8k context, avg output token length per generation call: 280 tokens, avg input tokens 30.
- Distribution: 75% short (<512 token) completions, 25% long flows; generation = 70% of token volume.
- HW baseline: 1 H100 node (configured with Redwood Dedicated runtime) ~ 9.2K tokens/sec for short completions at p95 ~ 160–180ms with batching disabled for low latency; with conservative batching we see 12–14K tokens/sec but latency increases.
- Safety headroom: 1.5x for steady-state to allow GC/maintenance windows + single-node failure tolerance; for bursts use autoscale to shared pool (2-node burst equivalent).

Questions for simulation:
1) Run per-node perf sim with the above mix and both quantization options (8-bit and 4-bit where applicable). Produce a tokens/sec curve vs p95 latency.
2) Validate tail behavior for 1–3 minute spikes to 120K tps across 6 nodes plus burst pool.
3) Show expected cost delta vs Dedicated + burst vs larger Dedicated commit (8 nodes) and recommended tradeoffs for procurement (capex vs opex).

Deliverable: a short table mapping tokens/sec bands to recommended committed nodes, expected p95 latencies, and fallback routing policy (model variant + hosted fallthrough).

Irene — can you coordinate with runtime to get the per-node sim and with solutions to draft the SOW line? Ben — can you draft the procurement-friendly summary once we have the numbers?

— Lauren

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Locke <ethan.locke@synthetixlabs.com>
Cc: Maria Gutierrez <maria.gutierrez@synthetixlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity plan and next steps for Dedicated commitment (Synthetix Labs)

Ethan / Maria — thanks for waiting while we ran the perf sims and cost options. Attached is a 1-page capacity summary plus the backup perf curves. TL;DR: we recommend a 6-node H100 Dedicated commit with a 2-node shared burst policy. Key numbers:
- Steady-state mapping: 45K tps steady -> 6 nodes with 1.5x steady headroom (safe steady capacity ~67.5K tps).
- Burst handling: 120K tps 1–3 minute spikes -> requires burst to add ~2 H100-equivalent slots; with that policy p95 gen latency during spike estimated ~280–350ms depending on request-size distribution.
- SLO fit: baseline p95 generation latency under steady load ~230ms. We can promise p95 < 300ms for steady-state in the SOW; burst p95 is expected to climb and we propose an explicit burst SLA clause and a fallback to a slightly lower-cost model variant (quantized) hosted in Redwood's regional pool as a controlled degradation.

Next steps:
1) Confirm model family and max context window (we assumed 8k).
2) Sign the Dedicated SOW (we'll send a DocuSign with the 6-node commitment + burst policy).
3) Schedule a security/compliance handoff for SOC2 and network onboarding (we've attached the onboarding checklist).

Attachments: synthetix_final_capacity_summary.pdf (capacity summary and perf curves), redwood_prelim_gpus_estimate.pdf (backup).

If these numbers look OK, Ben will prepare the procurement one-pager and Irene will attach the SOW wording. Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call to walk procurement through the tradeoffs.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
